claim: Flap impulse: ADDFLP reads PTIMUP — frames aloft — as the input to the vertical impulse, which is what makes lift DECAY the longer a bird hovers.

source.verbatim: ADDFLP	LDB	PTIMUP,U	NOW CALC GAINED Y VELOCITY

claim: Flap impulse: the multiplier is 256*96/255, which the assembler folds to 96. With MUL and the high-byte take on the next lines this yields (PTIMUP*96)>>8.

source.verbatim: LDA	#256*96/255	CALC NBR -96 TO 0 FROM 0 TO 255

claim: Flap impulse: TFR A,B then CLRA keeps only the HIGH byte of the 16-bit product — the >>8 of the impulse formula.
Flap impulse: SUBD #96 makes the result range from -96 (PTIMUP 0, strongest) to nearly 0 (PTIMUP 255, spent). DECIMAL.

source.verbatim: SUBD	#96		NEW DELTA-Y, USE IN GRAVITY CALC

claim: Flap impulse: ADDD PVELY — the impulse is ADDED to existing velocity, not assigned. A bird already falling at 500 flaps to 404, not to -96.
Flap steering: ASLA doubles the normalised joystick, so a flap moves the FLYX index by exactly +/-2 rungs.

Flap steering, the REJECTION clamp: BGT returns WITHOUT storing, so a result past +MAXVX leaves the index entirely UNCHANGED. This is rejection, not saturation — a player at +8 who flaps right stays at +8, and the top rung is reachable only from exactly one rung below. The branch comment reads 'BR=NO' and is inverted; trust the branch.

Flap steering: the mirror-image rejection for the negative bound — BLT past -MAXVX returns without storing. Note the rejection is HORIZONTAL only: the vertical impulse was already committed above, so a rejected flap still lifts.
PTIMUP: incremented once per airborne frame — the tick count that decays the flap impulse.

source.verbatim: AIRTIM	INC	PTIMUP,U	NBR OF TICKS IN THE AIR

claim: PTIMUP saturation: on overflow the counter is decremented straight back to 255 rather than wrapping. Wrapping would hand a fully-spent flapper a brand-new full-strength impulse.

source.verbatim: DEC	PTIMUP,U	NO OVERFLOW, JUST SATURATE

claim: Gravity pair: with the flap button HELD the gravity offset is CLEARED — wings down, GRAV alone. This is the glide.

source.verbatim: FLAPS2	CLRB			NO OFFSET TO GRAVITY

claim: Gravity pair: with the button RELEASED the offset is $04 — wings up, GRAV+4. Holding the button therefore exactly halves the fall rate. The pair is an OFFSET to GRAV, not two independent constants.

Gravity integration: ADDGRA adds the gravity byte to the 16-bit Y velocity, and ADDGRX then adds that velocity to the 8.8 Y position. No cap and no damping appear anywhere in the chain — there is no terminal velocity.

source.verbatim: ADDGRA	ADDB	GRAV		ADD IN VARIABLE GRAVITY

claim: Gravity: GRAV is initialised to 4. DECIMAL. Despite the 'VARIABLE GRAVITY' comment at the add site its only writer is this init.
FLYX ladder: the table STARTS here, four entries BEFORE the FLYX label, at index -8 = -$0200 (2 px/frame left). HEX, signed 16-bit.

FLYX ladder: the FLYX label sits on the ZERO entry, not the table start — the index is SIGNED and reads backwards for leftward flight. A transcription treating this label as element 0 and storing nine entries forward is wrong for EVERY leftward flight while reading like a sensible ladder. LNDXS3 has the same zero-point-label shape; it is a Williams house convention.
FLYX ladder: the final entry, index +8 = $0200. The rungs double at each step, giving +/-{2.0, 1.0, 0.5, 0.25, 0} px/frame — a non-linear ladder, not a linear velocity.
Flight X integration: the FLYX word is fetched by SIGNED index from the ladder base.

Flight X integration: the ladder word's LOW byte accumulates into PVELX+2, the sub-pixel accumulator that lives in the VELOCITY rather than the position. This is why X and Y use different position formats — only whole pixels ever reach PPOSX.

source.verbatim: ADDB	PVELX+2,U	ADD IN FRACTIONAL DISTANCE

claim: Flight X integration: ADCA #0 carries the sub-pixel overflow into the whole-pixel delta, which is what makes the shallow rungs advance a pixel every few frames instead of every frame.
Takeoff: a flap-initiated launch sets Y velocity to -$0080. HEX, negative meaning upward.
Takeoff: DEC PPOSY+1 lifts the entity one WHOLE pixel out of the landing band. Without this lift the entity re-lands on the same frame it took off.

source.verbatim: STKILL	DEC	PPOSY+1,U	JUMP UP 1 PIXEL (GET OUT OF LANDING AREA)

claim: Walk-off: STFALL clears the fractional distances but performs NO lift — the entity simply stops being supported, which is what makes stepping off a ledge feel different from jumping.
Walk-off: the initial Y velocity is ZERO. A walk-off is not an accelerating fall that has already begun.
Ground state machine: the STATE macro row is wait, animation call, three direction targets, and the FLYX index the state hands to flight on takeoff.
Ground state machine: PLYAR is the reversing state — 8 frames of REVR before settling to the standing state.
Ground state machine: PLYFR is the fastest run — 1 frame per step, and it hands FLYX index 8 to flight, the ladder's top rung.
Ground state machine: PLYMR is the last skid state, settling back toward standing. The skid chain is what gives a hard landing its slide.
Ground movement: ORRUN's rows pair an animation frame with a per-frame X delta; the first is the standstill-to-frame-1 entry with delta 0.

source.verbatim: ORRUN	FCB	RUN1,0		INITIAL FRAME FROM STANDSTILL TO FRAME 1

claim: Ground movement: the largest run delta is 3 pixels, on the frame-3-to-4 transition. The deltas 0/3/2/1/2 are what make the run cycle visibly uneven.

source.verbatim: FCB	RUN4,3		PIXEL JUMP FROM FRAME 3 TO 4 (PFRAME 2 TO 1)

claim: Ground movement: the skid frame carries an X delta of 2, packed with its picture index as SKID*256+2.

source.verbatim: LDD	#SKID*256+2	GET CORRECT DELTA X & PICTURE FOR SKID

claim: Landing conversion: FRCONV's first entry is the standing state — a landing at rest. The table maps incoming horizontal speed to a ground state.
Landing conversion: FRCONV's last entry is the fastest running state, so a bird landing at full speed keeps running rather than stopping dead.
Joust resolution: a skidding mount records PLANTZ 2 — it sits two pixels lower, which decides who wins a joust. jt1-5 records it; jt2 consumes it.

source.verbatim: LDB	#2		SKIDDING OSTRICH HAS A LANTZ 2 PIXELS LOWER

claim: Input contract: the two joystick direction bits are masked to $03 before normalisation.
Input contract: ASRA then SBCA #0 maps the raw bits to -1/0/+1. Notably raw 3 — BOTH directions held — normalises to 0, so a shell that implements 'last pressed wins' does not match the ROM.

Landing X map: LNDXS1 is ONE contiguous 352-byte table covering CRT pixel -$20 through $13F — not a family of per-wave variants. Confirmed by the RAM declarations LNDXD1 $20 + LNDXTB $140 = 352 (RAMDEF.SRC:376-378).
Landing X map: the first data row is CRT pixel -$20, i.e. the table's index origin is 32 pixels left of screen zero.
Landing X map: LNDXS3 is a LABEL INTO the table at the zero point, not a separate table — the same zero-point-label shape as FLYX.
Landing X map: LNDXS2 is the END MARKER immediately after the 352 bytes, exactly parallel to the RAM bound LNDXD2. The story's framing of LNDXS1/2/3 as three per-wave sources was wrong.
Background X map: BCKXS1 is the collision counterpart of LNDXS1, same 352-byte shape and origin.
Wave init: LNDXUP copies the ROM landing table into its RAM buffer at wave start.

Wave init: the copy ORs in bit 5 — 'FOR NOW, CLIFF 5 LANDS AT ALL POINTS'. Omitting this makes the bottom island unlandable outside its own X span, which surfaces as entities falling through the world. Per-cliff destruction is a later read-modify-write that only ever REMOVES bits.

source.verbatim: ORA	#$20		FOR NOW, CLIFF 5 LANDS AT ALL POINTS

claim: Ground test: CKGND ANDs the X-direction landing mask with the Y-direction one; the result is the mask the landing dispatch consumes.

source.verbatim: LDA	LNDXTB,X	STARTING TO LAND ON A CLIFF?

claim: Landing sets PTIMUP to 1, not zero — the "MINIMUM DOWN TIME" — so the first flap after touchdown is computed from timeUp=1 (STLDIR).
Walking off a ledge CLEARS PTIMUP (STFALL) — a saturated glide does not carry its spent impulse into the fall; the next flap is full strength.

source.verbatim: CLR	PTIMUP,U	NEEDS TO BE DONE

claim: Render: the visible raster is 292x240 pixels. EXTERNAL secondary source — the MAME williams driver states the board-level geometry the 1982 program source never does, so this is schema-only and never byte-opened. It is the logical backbuffer size the shell scales by an integer factor.

source.verbatim: (MAME williams driver williams.cpp:1556 — external secondary source: not in the vendored 1982 tree, schema-only, never byte-opened)
